The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below are three ways to create a **Google Cloud Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and boots from **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.  
Pick the one that best fits your workflow:

| Method | What you run | Where you run it |
|--------|--------------|------------------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Your terminal (with `gcloud` installed) |
| **REST API (curl)** | `curl -X POST …` | Any machine that can reach the Google APIs |
| **Python client** | `googleapiclient.discovery` | Your own Python script |

> **Important**  
> * The **RTX A6000** is only available in certain zones (e.g. `us-central1-a`, `us-east1-b`, `europe-west4-a`).  
> * The machine type must support GPUs (e.g. `n1-standard-8`, `n1-highmem-8`, `n1-highcpu-8`).  
> * After the instance is up, you’ll still need to install the NVIDIA driver (see the “Post‑create steps” section).

---

## 1. gcloud CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set variables
PROJECT="my-gcp-project"
ZONE="us-central1-a"          # pick a zone that supports RTX A6000
INSTANCE="rtx-a6000-ubuntu"
MACHINE="n1-standard-8"      # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
DISK_SIZE_GB=100             # boot disk size

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create "$INSTANCE" \
  --project="$PROJECT" \
  --zone="$ZONE" \
  --machine-type="$MACHINE" \
  --accelerator="type=$GPU_TYPE,count=$GPU_COUNT" \
  --image-family="ubuntu-2004-lts" \
  --image-project="ubuntu-os-cloud" \
  --boot-disk-size="$DISK_SIZE_GB" \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-standard \
  --metadata="install-nvidia-driver=true" \
  --tags="http-server,https-server" \
  --scopes="https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
```

> **Notes**  
> * `--metadata="install-nvidia-driver=true"` is a custom flag you can use in a startup script (see below).  
> * The `--tags` flag opens ports 80/443 if you want to run a web server.  
> * The `--scopes` flag gives the instance full Cloud Platform access; adjust as needed.

---

## 2. REST API (curl)

```bash
# 1️⃣  Get an OAuth 2.0 access token (replace with your own method)
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# 2️⃣  Build the JSON payload
cat <<EOF > instance.json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-standard"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      { "key": "install-nvidia-driver", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ]
}
EOF

# 3️⃣  POST the request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

> **Tip** – If you prefer a one‑liner, replace the `cat <<EOF … EOF` block with a single `-d` argument containing the JSON.

---

## 3. Python Client (google-api-python-client)

```python
from googleapiclient import discovery
from oauth2client.client import GoogleCredentials

# 1️⃣  Authenticate
credentials = GoogleCredentials.get_application_default()
service = discovery.build('compute', 'v1', credentials=credentials)

project = 'my-gcp-project'
zone = 'us-central1-a'
instance_name = 'rtx-a6000-ubuntu'

# 2️⃣  Build the instance body
instance_body = {
    'name': instance_name,
    'machineType': f'zones/{zone}/machineTypes/n1-standard-8',
    'disks': [{
        'boot': True,
        'initializeParams': {
            'sourceImage': 'projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts',
            'diskSizeGb': 100,
            'diskType': f'projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/diskTypes/pd-standard'
        }
    }],
    'networkInterfaces': [{
        'network': 'global/networks/default',
        'accessConfigs': [{'type': 'ONE_TO_ONE_NAT', 'name': 'External NAT'}]
    }],
    'accelerators': [{
        'acceleratorType': f'projects/{project}/zones/{zone}/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-a6000',
        'acceleratorCount': 1
    }],
    'metadata': {
        'items': [{'key': 'install-nvidia-driver', 'value': 'true'}]
    },
    'serviceAccounts': [{
        'email': 'default',
        'scopes': ['https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform']
    }]
}

# 3️⃣  Insert the instance
operation = service.instances().insert(
    project=project,
    zone=zone,
    body=instance_body
).execute()

print(f'Instance creation started: {operation["name"]}')
```

---

## Post‑Create Steps (GPU Driver)

Google Cloud does **not** automatically install the NVIDIA driver for you.  
After the instance is running, SSH into it and run:

```bash
# Update package lists
sudo apt-get update

# Install the NVIDIA driver (recommended version for A6000)
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535

# Reboot to load the driver
sudo reboot
```

> **Alternative** – Use the `install-nvidia-driver=true` metadata key and a startup script that runs the above commands automatically.

---

### Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| ✅ | Zone supports RTX A6000 |
| ✅ | Machine type supports GPUs |
| ✅ | GPU type set to `nvidia-a6000` |
| ✅ | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| ✅ | Boot disk size ≥ 100 GB (recommended) |
| ✅ | Install NVIDIA driver after boot |
| ✅ | Proper IAM scopes / service account |

Feel free to copy/paste the snippet that matches your workflow and tweak the variables (`PROJECT`, `ZONE`, `INSTANCE`, etc.) to fit your environment. Happy GPU computing!
